newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends flat to up in tight trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends flat to up in tight trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished flat to slightly higher Thursday as the complex continued to meander within its recent trading range.
"It's a lazy market. No one wants to do anything," said a Denver-based futures trader.
Strength in the western cash market tied to several unplanned plant outages this week failed to stir buying interest in most futures players, market sources said.
Firm, peak power prices for day-ahead delivery at COB tightened to a $12.00-12.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) range and those at PV rose $1 to $15.00-16.00
Neither were players moved by another drop in natural gas futures today. The NYMEX March Henry Hub gas contract finished down 9.1 cents at $1.999 per million British thermal units.
In the western gas market, March deliveries at the Sumas export point on the U.S./Canada border were notionally valued at $1.40-$1.50 and at the San Juan Basin area in the Southwest $1.56-$1.62.
The spot Palo Verde (PV) and California-Oregon Border (COB) futures contracts were both locked in a 15 cent range.
March COB settled up five cents at $10.85 aftering posting a high of $11.00. April COB ended up 15 cents at $10.15.
March PV settled up 11 cents at $13.35, near the day's high of $13.40. Most other active PV months finished the session unchanged from yesterday's settlements.
Two generating units -- the 750 megawatt (MW) Navajo unit 2 in Arizona and 500 MW Jim Bridger unit 1 in Wyoming -- were expected to resume operation tonight after boiler tube repair.
The 550 MW Laramie River Station coal-fired power unit 3 in Wheatland, Wyo., to resume service late Friday following a shutdown on Tuesday for a boiler tube leak.
Two other units in the West were still shut, and their restart remained unknown.

The 1,100 MW pumped storage hydroelectric Helms plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut Feb 1 for mechanical repairs, and the 187 MW unit 2 at the Four Corners plant was still down because of a tube leak.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were forecast to average three to six degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Sunday as showers would continue at times across the the region with chance of snow showers in the inland area.
In the Southwest, readings would average two to four degrees above normal and climb as high as eight degrees above normal Sunday.
NYMEX estimated 137 COB and 404 PV contracts were sold, compared with Wednesday's sale of 150 COB and 194 PV lots.
